Two strategy families documented: (1) pullback-reversal (needs trend line + candlestick pattern + oscillator divergence, subjective/discretionary, similar implementability issue as RSI-divergence -019); (2) pivot-level breakout (concrete, mechanical): wait for price to CLOSE above/below a pivot level (P, R1, R2, R3, S1, S2, S3) signaling a new trend emerging, go long/short accordingly, stop beyond the next pivot level, target at 2:1 R:R.
notes: Implementing the mechanically-testable breakout variant (close crosses above the DAILY pivot point P, computed from the prior day's H/L/C, signals a long entry; exit when close crosses back below P) rather than the discretionary pullback-reversal variant. First Pivot Point (classic floor-trader P/R/S levels derived from prior-session HLC) strategy tested in this repo -- distinct from every prior indicator since it uses NO smoothing/lookback window at all, purely the single prior bar's H/L/C algebraically combined.

Multiple converging sources (AlchemyMarkets, Aron Groups, GrandAlgo, Orbex, StrefaTradingu) describe the classic (Linda Bradford Raschke / Laurence Connors, 1995) Turtle Soup mean-reversion pattern: price makes a new 20-day low (or high) -- the 'false breakout' of a Donchian-style 20-bar extreme originally used by Turtle traders as an entry signal -- then FAILS to continue and reverses back inside the prior range. Long setup (fading a failed breakdown): price closes below the 20-day low, then the very next close moves back ABOVE that 20-day low level, signaling the breakdown was a stop-hunt/false move; exit on a fixed target or opposite signal. Explicitly a COUNTER-TREND mean-reversion pattern (per TradingView snippet): 'in strong trending regimes, false signals increase; in consolidation/range-bound conditions it works better' -- an explicit caveat about regime-dependence.
notes: Concrete, well-corroborated (originally by Connors 1995 per Captain Trading, popularized as ICT 'Turtle Soup') rule: fade the failed breakdown of a rolling 20-day low. Distinct from every existing Donchian/breakout strategy in this repo (-008, -054, which trade IN THE DIRECTION of the breakout) -- this is the exact INVERSE, betting on breakout FAILURE rather than continuation. First explicitly counter-trend/mean-reversion breakout-fade strategy tested in this repo.
